title: Rotate Square Matrix
statement:
Rotate a square matrix a quarter turn clockwise, in place.

Contract
- `matrix` is non-null and square: it has `n` rows and each row has `n` columns. `n` may be 0.
- After the call, the value that started at row `r`, column `c` must be at row `c`, column `n - 1 - r`.
- Modify `matrix` itself and return nothing; do not build a second n x n matrix.

Examples
- `{{1,2},{3,4}}` becomes `{{3,1},{4,2}}`.
- `{{1,2,3},{4,5,6},{7,8,9}}` becomes `{{7,4,1},{8,5,2},{9,6,3}}`.
- `{{5}}` stays `{{5}}`.
hints: Write down where a single cell goes: the value at (r, c) lands at (c, n - 1 - r). Copying into a new matrix works but uses O(n^2) space.
A quarter turn can be built from two simpler reflections of the whole grid. Try combining a flip across the main diagonal with another flip.
Swap across the main diagonal, then reverse every row, using only a few temporary variables. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the side length of the matrix.
inputSyntax: Input: a square matrix as nested lists of integers, for example: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]
